 Politiko Lokal San Miguel, Leyte seeks state of calamity declaration over severe drought, P11.6-M agri loss
 The local government here has recommended declaring a state of calamity across the municipality following a severe dry spell that has plagued the town for over six months, leaving millions of pesos in agricultural damage and triggering a severe water shortage.
 By Politiko Staff October 21, 2026 7:47 PM By Politiko staff 
 The local government here has recommended declaring a state of calamity across the municipality following a severe dry spell that has plagued the town for over six months, leaving millions of pesos in agricultural damage and triggering a severe water shortage.
 “’Yung bayan ng San Miguel, Leyte, nakararanas po kami ngayon ng tagtuyot. Severe and prolonged drought. Mahigit anim na buwan na po ‘yung nararanasan namin,” San Miguel Mayor Norman Sabdao said in an interview on Bilyonaryo News Channel’s program Politiko Nightly.
 Data from the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (MDRRMC) showed that agricultural losses and damage reached P11.6 million due to the prolonged heat.
 Aside from devastating local crop production, the drought has severely disrupted the town’s potable water supply.
 “Hirap na hirap po talaga kami ngayon sa supply ng tubig. That’s the main reason bakit bumaba at malaki po ‘yung nawala sa produksyon namin sa agrikultura,” Sabdao explained.
 “Bagama’t meron po kaming Level 3 Waterworks System, as of now, ito ay hindi nagbibigay sa amin ng tamang supply kaya po nakaasa po kami ngayon sa mga deep well po at saka sa mga jetmatic pumps,” he added.
 Prompted by the worsening impact on residents and livelihoods, Sabdao submitted a formal recommendation to the Sangguniang Bayan to place the entire municipality under a state of calamity.
 “Kaya po inirekomenda na rin po namin sa Sangguniang Bayan na magdeklara na po at ipailalim na po ‘yung bayan ng San Miguel, Leyte sa State of Calamity para po makagawa po kami ng tamang hakbang or timely interventions sa mga magsasaka po namin na totally affected sa prolonged and severe drought,” Sabdao said.
 “Ganu’n din po sa supply ng tubig namin na hirap na hirap po ‘yung mga mamamayan namin na makakuha po ng supply ng tubig,” he added.
 Once approved by the municipal council, the declaration will allow the local government unit to unleash quick response funds (QRF) and relief measures to cushion the impact of the crisis.
 The full interview with Sabdao aired during the Oct. 20 episode of “Politiko Nightly.” The program airs Monday through Friday at 9:00 p.m. on Free TV Channel 31, Cignal Channel 24, Samsung TV Plus, TCL Smart TVs, Blast TV, AmasianTV, Cignal Play, and BNC’s YouTube and Facebook channels. —Politiko.com.ph
